newsitem.title: USA: Electronic Designs hurt by memory chip.
newsitem.headline: Electronic Designs hurt by memory chip.

text.p: Electronic Designs Inc said Tuesday its third quarter results were hurt by weakness in the memory chip market.

The company said income from continuing operations for the third quarter of fiscal 1997 was $1.2 million, or $0.14 per share, compared with $1.4 million, or $0.16 per share for the same period last year.

"EDI continues to be adversely affected by the price weakness in the memory chip market," said chief executive Don McGuinness. "While we have seen evidence of price stability returning to the memory market, aggressive pricing continues to pressure sales and margins," he said.

"With the anticipated completion of the divestiture of the Crystallume Division this quarter, EDI will be focused solely on growing its core businesses. We are beginning to realize the benefits of our new product introductions coupled with increasing sales in the display market, providing positive momentum for the balance of fiscal year 1997," he added.
